what: Aggregate wall throughput across every concurrency rung measured on this model, for one and two B70s, with and without speculation. Assembled from five campaigns; no new GPU time.
metric: aggregate_tok_s_wall from the concurrency-oracle ladder, median over passes, 128-token responses, temperature 0, ignore_eos, 2026-08-25 small-context suite
pass_policy: Pass 1 of every ladder is discarded. It is warmup-contaminated at low concurrency - the TP1 depth-3 pass 1 reads c2 at 134.1 tok/s, below its own c1 at 158.8, against 300.8 in pass 2.

matrix_tok_s.note_on_tp1_c36_to_c56: c36, c40, c44, c48 and c56 in the TP1 columns are x2 (2026-09-09, ten passes, every rung in the capture set, max_num_seqs 64, max_num_batched_tokens 512). x2 also re-read c32 (1593.4 / 1153.1) and c64 (1726.9 / 1201.4), within 0.2% of the pooled values kept in those rows.
matrix_tok_s.r293_columns: Columns 6-9 (2026-09-11): the same ladders on the R293 image with VLLM_XPU_FP16_LINEAR_CLASSPAD=1 (arms r1, r2; four passes, pass 1 discarded). c96/c128 pending r6/r7. The R224 columns 2-5 are the published lane; see 2026-09-11-qwen35-4b-r290-classpad-on-the-server.json.

readings.crossover: Both topologies cross between c16 and c20. On one card speculation leads by 2.8% at c16 and trails by 14.4% at c20; on two cards it leads by 5.9% at c16 and trails by 18.3% at c20. The ceiling is a property of the concurrency, not of the card count.
readings.single_user: Depth 3 is worth 1.56x on one card (159.2 against 101.9) and 1.67x on two (227.3 against 136.3).
readings.peak_aggregate: The highest aggregate measured anywhere in this campaign is 3103.9 tok/s, two cards without speculation at c128, and it is still rising. On one card the peak is 1810.9 at c128. Two cards without speculation at c128 is 1.71x one card at the same rung, against 1.36x at c32 and c64 - the second card helps more the more concurrency there is.
readings.speculation_stops_scaling: Depth 3 on one card is flat from c16 to c128 - 1088.9 to 1166.6, a 7% gain over an eightfold increase in users - while no-speculation rises 1058.8 to 1810.9, a 71% gain.
readings.second_card: TP2 over TP1 is 1.34x to 1.61x depending on rung and mode, with the largest gains at c32 and c64 where a single card is closer to saturation.
readings.r293: With the class-consistent FP16 linear the no-speculation column keeps rising and the depth-3 column no longer stalls: one card depth 3 reads 1353 at c16 (R224 1089) and 1831 at c64 (1201); two cards 1862 and 2694 (1588, 2021). The speculation crossover moves from c16-c20 to about c32 on one card (depth 3 1608 against MTP0 1625 at c32) and c24-c32 on two. Below c8 the pad path costs 5-11%.

caveats.mixed_server_configs_at_high_rungs: c96 and c128 come only from f4, which ran max_num_seqs 128 and max_num_batched_tokens 1024 against the 64/512 used elsewhere, and c64 pools f1, f4 and v1. Those settings materially change the divergence rate but barely change throughput - f1 and f4 read 1201.0 and 1217.2 at depth-3 c64, and 1723.0 and 1732.5 without speculation - so the throughput matrix tolerates the mix. An identity comparison would not.
caveats.tp2_above_c64_unmeasured: CLOSED by t7, which ran TP2 at c64, c96 and c128 with f4's settings so the two columns are comparable at those rungs. The remaining gaps are minor: TP2 was never run at c1-c4 with these settings, and TP2 has not been run between c40 and c64 (TP1 now has c36 through c56 from x2).
caveats.identity_is_elsewhere: This is throughput only. The identity rates at these rungs, and the reasons the depth-3 column stops scaling, are in 2026-09-09-qwen35-4b-speculation-ceiling-is-c16.json and 2026-09-09-qwen35-4b-beyond-c64.json.

a_non_monotone_dip_at_c40.statement: Aggregate throughput is not monotone in concurrency. Without speculation, one card reads 1595 tok/s at c32, 1360 at c40 and 1732 at c64 - a 15% drop going from 32 to 40 concurrent users, recovering by 64.
a_non_monotone_dip_at_c40.why_it_is_believable: Two independent arms measured c40 and agree to 0.1% (1360.8 and 1359.2), against a c32 pair that also agrees to 0.1% (1596.0 and 1594.0). Throughput is the tightest measurement on this lane - the g1/g2 replicate reproduces it to a tenth of a percent - so a 15% gap is far outside anything the measurement can manufacture.
a_non_monotone_dip_at_c40.speculation_shows_it_too: Depth 3 reads 1136.5 and 1156.3 at c32 against 1142.3 and 1156.6 at c40, so the dip is much smaller there - the speculative path is already throughput-limited by c32 and has less to lose.
a_non_monotone_dip_at_c40.not_explained: 32 and 64 are powers of two and 40 is not, which points at a tiling or occupancy effect in the decode kernels, but nothing here tests that. c40 is captured in the graph set, so it is not an uncaptured-shape fallback.
a_non_monotone_dip_at_c40.why_it_was_found: c40 exists in these arms only because it was added to give a GDN-group-of-32 hypothesis somewhere to show up. No previous ladder on this lane measured it.
a_non_monotone_dip_at_c40.operational: Sizing a server for 40 concurrent users would be measurably worse than sizing it for either 32 or 64. Rungs between the usual powers of two are worth measuring before a capacity decision.
a_non_monotone_dip_at_c40.superseded: See the_dip_is_at_c36 below: x2 mapped the region at every rung and the cliff is at 32->36, not at 40. The c40 reading itself reproduced a third time to 0.1% (1360.0).

the_dip_is_at_c36.arm: x2: TP1, rungs 32/36/40/44/48/56/64, ten passes each, both lanes, with every rung in the cudagraph capture set (1,2,4,8,16,24,32,36,40,44,48,52,56,60,64) so no rung pads to a larger captured shape.
the_dip_is_at_c36.shape: Not a dip at 40. A 21.4% cliff between c32 and c36, then a monotone, roughly linear recovery: each four extra users add about 80-115 tok/s until c64 is 8.4% above c32. c40 reads 1360.0, the third arm to put it within 0.1% of 1360.
the_dip_is_at_c36.padding_is_eliminated: Every rung was a captured shape and the server log confirms the capture set, so the previous candidate - an uncaptured c36 padding to 40 and c44 to 50 - cannot be the cause. The dip is a property of the arithmetic at those row counts, not of graph replay.
the_dip_is_at_c36.identity_at_these_rungs: MTP0 stays near-exact through the region: 319/320, 358/360, 400/400, 439/440, 478/480, 558/560, 633/640. Depth 3 runs 5-14% divergent as it does everywhere above c16.

the_candidate.statement: One thing in this server has exactly this shape. The R224 overlay runs every unquantized FP16 linear - the vocabulary projection and the MTP fc - in pieces of at most VLLM_XPU_FP16_LINEAR_ROWCHUNK rows, default 32. At c36 the last piece holds 4 rows; at c40, 8; c44, 12; c48, 16; c56, 24; c64, 32 (two full pieces). Throughput rises monotonically with the size of that tail piece and is back to a clean value exactly where the tail is full.
the_candidate.the_depth3_lane_agrees: At depth 3 each sequence contributes four rows per step, so c32 is already four full pieces. The only rungs whose row count leaves a partial piece are c36 (144 rows: four full plus 16) and c44 (176: five plus 16), and those are the only two rungs where the depth-3 column dips (1102.2 and 1143.5 against 1153.1-1201.4 elsewhere). Rungs with no tail (c40 = 160, c48 = 192, c56 = 224, c64 = 256) do not dip.
the_candidate.status: HYPOTHESIS, under test in chain 11 (y1: the same rungs with the chunk disabled; y2: the prediction that with the chunk on the next cliff is at c68 and is gone by c96; y3: that the 5 ms stagger recipe stays exact with the chunk off). Not a finding until y1 reports.
the_candidate.why_it_matters: The chunk was added for batch invariance and every server in this lane and the 27B and 9B lanes runs it. If it is the cause, every no-speculation rung that is not a multiple of 32 pays up to 21% for it, and every published exact-throughput figure at c16/c32/c64/c96/c128 happens to sit where the cost is zero.
